vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: polito-notes
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a legitimate tool designed to automate the conversion of PDF lecture slides into bilingual (Italian and English) markdown notes for university courses. It defines a clear workflow for text extraction using standard tools like pdftotext and organizes output into a specific local directory structure (~/Documenti/github/polito/). The instructions in SKILL.md are focused entirely on academic note-taking quality and structure, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (converting PDFs into bilingual markdown notes and writing them into a course folder); it reads and writes local files but does not request unrelated credentials or network calls.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (convert lecture PDFs into Italian+English markdown notes placed in course folders) matches the instructions: extract PDF text, determine course folder, check existing notes, and write notes.md and notes-en.md. Required actions (reading the PDF, checking repository folders, writing files) are appropriate for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to read PDFs, list and inspect ~/Documenti/github/polito/ course folders, read existing notes to integrate content, and write new/updated files into those folders. That aligns with the goal but is broad: the skill will read existing local notes and may modify or overwrite files. It also enforces a strict 'zero information loss' rule (copy all definitions/formulas), which could reproduce all content from any provided PDF, including sensitive material if present.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or third-party downloads. It suggests using pdftotext or a Python script for extraction but does not install anything itself. This is low risk from an install/execution perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. All required accesses are local filesystem operations (reading the provided PDF and existing notes, writing new markdown files), which are proportionate to the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and autonomous invocation is not disabled (the platform default). The skill does not request persistent platform-wide privileges or to modify other skills. Its filesystem writes are limited to the course-note folders described in the doc, which is appropriate for its purpose but should be run with user consent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose, but before installing or running it consider the following: 1) It reads and writes files under ~/Documenti/github/polito/ (the SKILL.md uses an Italian path). Make sure that path is correct for you; otherwise the agent may create unexpected folders or fail. 2) The workflow will read existing notes to integrate new content and will write notes.md and notes-en.md — back up any existing notes you care about to avoid accidental overwrites. 3) The 'Zero information loss' rule means the skill will reproduce everything from the PDF (formulas, examples, caveats). Do not feed PDFs containing private or sensitive data unless you intend those contents to be fully duplicated into markdown. 4) The skill expects pdftotext or a Python extraction script to be available; if those binaries/tools are missing the agent may fail or ask you to install them. 5) Test on a small, non-sensitive lecture PDF first to confirm output style and file-placement behavior. If you need networked storage or different folder locations, verify/adjust the target path before running. Overall, the skill is internally consistent and does not request unrelated credentials or external endpoints, but exercise standard caution with local file writes and sensitive input.
